basics.name: Terence Kearns
basics.label: Solutions Architect
basics.summary: Solutions Architect and co-founder with three decades studying and building information systems. Designs and ships software that maps business workflows to durable systems—from campus-scale media platforms to multi-cloud product stacks. Currently building NDX’s dual track: grassroots micro-apps and Sentinel BI / SBI Dashboard consultancy.

work.name: NDX Pty Ltd
work.summary: Software solutions for grassroots and enterprise markets on a multi-cloud stack.
highlights: Ship Work Hours Online (Deno Fresh), a mobile-first time and multiplier calculator, as a pre-beta grassroots wedge toward beta and monetization.
Build Sentinel BI for internal use and package SBI Dashboard consultancy so managers get an at-a-glance org view that opens the door to deeper Sentinel orchestration.
Operate a multi-cloud delivery stack—self-hosted Kubernetes, Cloudflare Workers, and AWS—for software aimed at both grassroots and enterprise markets.

work.name: University of Canberra
work.summary: Campus systems including lecture streaming, data warehouse integration, and policy document management.
highlights: Built the campus Lecture Streaming System (2003): automated livestream and video archive with a lecturer web UI, enrollment-aware student portal views, and data-warehouse feeds.

Ran capture on 7 on-premise hosts (4 video cards each) wired into lecture halls; wrote a C#/.NET central server (“Snow White”) and Windows services that drove Windows Media Encoder state machines on each host, plus CLI archive jobs.
Built the university Policy database, a custom document management app on a bespoke XML stack (XAO PHP), with substantial XML/XSLT work across university systems.

work.name: Australian Electrical and Electronics Manufacturers Association (AEEMA)
highlights: Built a database-driven website and CMS in ColdFusion before off-the-shelf CMS products were common.

work.name: Department of Defence
highlights: Built and graphically designed the main Australian Army website; coordinated unit sites and liaised with their creators.
Oversaw implementation of Defence’s first corporate CMS (ASP.NET) delivered with an external Brisbane web studio.
Applied SGML and early XML in a documents-focused Defence department while owning ongoing Army web delivery before and after the CMS.
